variety/memo: A model that overfits has memorized its training images, quirks and all. One fix: never show it exactly the same image twice.
variety/change: Each time an image is used, change it a little at random. Shift it, make it brighter or darker, crop it. It still shows the same thing, so its label stays true.
variety/flip: But the change must keep the label true. Flip this right arrow left to right and it points left: now its label is wrong. A flipped photo of a cat is still a cat.
variety/which: So which changes are safe depends on the task. A six turned upside down is a nine, and a red light with its colors shifted can look green.
crops/count: Random crops alone add a lot. A twenty eight pixel crop fits at five places across a thirty two pixel image, and five down: twenty five crops.
crops/flips: Add a random flip, and every image comes in fifty versions.
crops/train: Do this only while training, with fresh random choices every time. Validation and test images stay untouched, so they still measure the model on real data.
crops/gap: The training loss ends a little higher, because varied images are harder to memorize, and the validation loss ends lower: a smaller gap.
